findings.problem: RULE-CAT-053 refuses every write under an inactive Item, and REQ-CAT-130 refuses reactivation until the ACTIVE-state invariants hold. The two together leave three states the user can never leave. (1) 0 active Variants: generation is refused and Variants have no reactivation. (2) An inactive Category: PUT categoryFk is refused and Categories have no reactivation. (3) A BUNDLE with an invalid component: API-CAT-017 is refused. The RULE-CAT-050 and RULE-CAT-026 messages offer next actions that cannot be taken. This is the same pattern in three places.
findings.fix: In a new ADR, amend RULE-CAT-053 and REQ-CAT-135 so three repair operations stay allowed on an inactive Item: Variant generation (API-CAT-006), a categoryFk-only change (API-CAT-003) and replacing the Bundle components (API-CAT-017). Each is still subject to its own rules. Update SRS A7, the API-CAT-003/006/017 Validations and Orchestration lines, and the CAT-422-PARENT-INACTIVE trigger.

findings.clause: consistent (F3 SCR-CAT-001 inactive Item read-only; ui-ux-spec)
findings.problem: On an inactive Item, F3 and the UX spec hide exactly the affordances that the REQ-CAT-130 refusals direct the user to use.
findings.fix: On an inactive Item's Entry, keep 'Generate variants' (while `variants` is on), the Category field and the Bundle components pane available. Everything else stays read-only. Link the ITEM-STATE-COMMAND refusal banners to these affordances.

findings.problem: These TCs assert the refusal but never prove that the Item can recover.
findings.fix: Extend each TC with its repair step, then a reactivation that succeeds. Add a frontend TC showing that the three affordances remain on an inactive Item.

findings.problem: API-CAT-024 locks only the Category row before counting its children. API-CAT-021 and API-CAT-023 read the parent unlocked, under the tree lock, and API-CAT-024 never takes the tree lock. A parallel sub-category create or move can therefore commit an active child under an inactive parent, which RULE-CAT-023 forbids.
findings.fix: Have API-CAT-024 take pg_advisory_xact_lock (TENANT_ID, 'CAT_CATEGORY_TREE') before QR-CAT-038. Amend ADR-CAT-047. Add an AC and a parallel-request TC (create a child and deactivate its parent at the same time): exactly one succeeds.

findings.problem: Category, Variant attribute and attribute value can be deactivated but never reactivated. Their codes are unique across active and inactive rows (UQ_CAT_CATEGORY_CODE, UQ_CAT_VAR_ATTR_CODE and UQ_CAT_VAR_ATTR_VALUE_CODE are not partial). A mistaken deactivation therefore loses the record and its code permanently, and a deactivated tree node cannot come back.
findings.fix: Add a reactivation for each: PATCH {isActiveFl:true}, guarded by RULE-CAT-023/024 for Categories (parent active, sibling name free) and RULE-CAT-016 for attributes and values. Add a REQ, AC, API block, catalog codes and TCs for each. This also gives G1 case (2) a second way out.

findings.clause: "C5 Every user-maintained code list is an MDL lookup type …" / "F3 … a module 'types' table"
findings.problem: CAT_VAR_ATTR and CAT_VAR_ATTR_VALUE are user-maintained code lists (code, nameAr, nameEn, sortOrder, isActiveFl) stored in module tables. ADR-CAT-003/018 justify them against C-GIVEN-1 only, and no ADR answers C5/F3 the way ADR-CAT-042 answers F5.
findings.fix: Add an ADR showing why mdl cannot hold them: tenant-defined types, values nested per attribute, and FK integrity from assignments (FK_CAT_VAR_ATTR_ASSIGN_CAT_VAR_ATTR_VALUE). If mdl lacks tenant-created types, raise CORE-GAP-tenant-lookup-types.md.

findings.clause: P3 read-binding (cross-screen jump identifies one record)
findings.problem: The RULE-CAT-003 next action jumps to /cat/items?text=<nameAr>. That search is a substring LIKE, while the duplicate check compares normalised names, so the jump can list several Items or miss the duplicate. The backend promises 'the existing Item's code' as the next action, but neither LocalizedError nor the message carries it (ADR-CAT-052 §5).
findings.fix: Add {code} to the RULE-CAT-003 message, as RULE-CAT-029 already does, filled from QR-CAT-002. Make the frontend jump to /cat/items?text=<code>. Mark AC-CAT-007, TC-CAT-003 and TC-CAT-126 MODIFIED.

findings.clause: "C13 One PermissionContributor (<Module>Permissions)…"; "F2 A native query without TENANT_ID"
findings.problem: PHASE CORE names the contributor CatPermissions, while Given usage, SEC-BE and bootstrap name it CatPermissionContributor. The default-sortOrder sub-selects in QR-CAT-024, 029 and 034 (MAX(SORT_ORDER)+1 inside an INSERT) carry no TENANT_ID, and an INSERT…SELECT has to be native.
findings.fix: Use one name, CatPermissions, implementing PermissionContributor. Compute the default sortOrder in a tenant-filtered JPQL read before the save, or add TENANT_ID = :tenant and @TenantUnscoped.

findings.problem: CORE-GAP-in-process-authorization exists only in the ADR folder. No OPEN platform-finding row records it with an owner.
findings.fix: Add an OPEN row. Owner: erp-core. Evidence: C13, F9, ADR-CAT-061, ADR-CAT-066 and the CORE-GAP file, with its three options.

findings.problem: The backend plan's header omits frontend TC-CAT-208 and 209. ADR-CAT-052 still quotes '124 of 129' and '52' ACs.
findings.fix: Add 208–209 to the header's frontend range. Add a note to ADR-CAT-052 that its counts are superseded: 146 backend ACs, 152 combined.

findings.problem: A synchronous import of up to 5,000 rows runs in one transaction, allocates codes row by row and holds the tenant scale-prefix lock throughout. No time budget or timeout is stated.
findings.fix: State a target duration and the request timeout. Allocate codes in batches. Take the prefix lock once per import. Name what happens when the timeout is exceeded.

findings.problem: Only TC-CAT-198 (backend) and TC-CAT-209 (frontend) exercise RULE-CAT-053.
findings.fix: Add one parameterised TC over API-CAT-003, 006, 008, 010, 012, 014, 015, 017, 018 and 019 under an inactive parent. It also asserts that child deactivations still succeed and, after G1, that the three repair operations succeed.

findings.problem: The ItemStateRequest schema allows both fields, an empty body or isActiveFl false.
findings.fix: Set isActiveFl enum [true] and add oneOf (or minProperties/maxProperties 1) in the plan, then regenerate the spec.
